clue.text: Hard wood to chop into small pieces

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
ash is a kind of timber, from the tree of that name

explanation.surface: A tough piece of timber that someone must cut up small.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym as a verb: cooks do this to potatoes or meat when they dice them finely.

clue.text: Beer that causes fat under surface of skin?

indicators.note: in a down clue the plump word sits below the single letter
the surface of a word is its outside edge, here taken as its opening letter

parts.note: tubby is an informal word for fat or plump

explanation.surface: A warning that drinking ale lays down a layer of flab just beneath the skin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surface of' takes the first letter of skin and 'under' places the word for fat beneath it. The answer is Australian slang for a small squat bottle of beer.
explanation.definitionFit: An example by slang: in Australia it names a short squat bottle of lager.

clue.text: The phantom or spirit ignored by audience

indicators.note: an audience listens, so the phrase is taken as it is heard rather than as it is spelt

parts.note: Scotch is a spirit (whisky) and missed means ignored or overlooked

explanation.surface: A ghost, or perhaps a soul, that the theatre crowd pays no attention to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by audience' tells us to say 'Scotch missed' and write what we hear. 'Spirit' looks like a ghost beside 'phantom'; it is whisky.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: British speakers use it sarcastically for something imagined or insubstantial, as well as for a fine drizzle.

clue.text: Duck round, dropping off two-wheeler

indicators.note: the rider falls from the vehicle, so that letter leaves the word

parts.note: a scooter is a small vehicle with two wheels
the letter O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Someone crouches as they go round a bend and tumbles from their bike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping off' removes one O, the round letter, from the vehicle. 'Duck' reads as a verb; it is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: it is a dark sea-going species of the bird.

clue.text: Devilry is found in motorway controller

indicators.note: says that the word 'is' sits inside the letters of the other two pieces

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for motorway, as in the British M1
a chief is the person in control

explanation.surface: Something wicked is discovered inside the person who runs the highway.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: both mean playful or wicked troublemaking.

clue.text: Exaggerated love for a German

parts.note: OTT, short for over the top, means exaggerated
love is a score of nil in tennis, written O

explanation.surface: Overblown passion directed at a man from Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: it is a typical man's first name in Germany.

clue.text: Areas of growth that revived rare habit (almost)

indicators.note: revived suggests the letters are given new life in a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: almost says the word falls just short, losing its final letter

parts.note: taken as written, less its last letter

explanation.surface: Parts of the economy picking up have brought back a custom that had nearly died out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims habit to HABI, and 'revived' rearranges RARE with HABI. The definition is loose: these are collections of plants.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose plural description: they are collections of preserved plants, or the rooms that hold them.

clue.text: Six hours is the deadline for paying the rent

definitions.meaning: six hours are one fourth of the twenty-four

definitions.text: the deadline for paying the rent
definitions.meaning: in Britain rents traditionally fall due on four fixed dates a year, such as Lady Day and Michaelmas

explanation.definitionFit: Literally a fourth of twenty-four hours, and as a British term one of four dates when rents fall due.

clue.text: Investigating officer chasing a quantity unknown to montezuma, for example

indicators.note: chasing puts the detective behind the other two letters

parts.note: Z is one of the letters algebra uses for an unknown
tec is old slang for a detective

explanation.surface: A detective is on the trail of some amount that the emperor never knew about.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: he was emperor of this Mexican people when the Spanish arrived.

clue.text: A true cocktail chaser for mint liqueur

indicators.note: a chaser follows another drink, so the mixed letters come after the other piece

parts.note: to mint money is to coin it

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A proper mixed drink to follow a minty after-dinner tipple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cocktail' rearranges A TRUE to give TREAU, and 'chaser for' places it behind the word for mint. 'Mint' looks like a flavour; it is the verb for making money.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: it is a French orange-flavoured brand of the drink.

clue.text: Environment partially protected by Panama

indicators.note: what is protected is covered, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a panama is a kind of straw hat
partially means a bit, to some extent

explanation.surface: Wildlife surroundings that the Central American state shields to some degree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'protected by' puts A BIT inside the headgear. 'Panama' looks like the country; it is the straw hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: the natural surroundings in which a creature lives.

clue.text: How one might force entry and brag to the lawyers

parts.note: to crow is to boast
the Bar is the collective name for barristers

explanation.surface: A burglar breaks in and then boasts about it to their legal team.
explanation.definitionFit: A description by use: it is the iron lever a burglar jemmies a door with.

clue.text: Put off one's stroke by somewhat tipsy chef

indicators.note: somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A slightly drunk cook distracts a player in the middle of a shot.
explanation.definitionFit: A sporting sense: to unsettle an opponent mentally, usually with 'out', so that they play badly.

clue.text: Job writing to a finish?

parts.note: a post is a job or position
script is handwriting or written text

explanation.surface: A piece of written work that must be seen through to the end.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines the answer: the words added after the close of a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A whimsical description: it is the extra note tacked on after the close of a letter.

clue.text: What one does with expenses when beer and rum is drunk

indicators.note: a drunk is unsteady and muddled, so the letters are muddled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: How someone treats the company account once the ale and spirits have been downed.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: an employer pays back what staff have spent.

clue.text: Telegraph on pointed barrier to progress

indicators.note: on simply joins the two words, one attached to the other

parts.note: barbed means having sharp points, and a barbed remark is a pointed one
to wire is to send a telegram, and a wire is a telegram

explanation.surface: The newspaper comments sharply on something that is holding the country back.
explanation.definitionFit: A description: spiked fencing strung up to stop people or animals getting through.

clue.text: Simple attacking player given to occasional hand of poker

indicators.note: the second word is added to the first one

parts.note: a straight, five cards in sequence, is a hand that turns up now and then in poker
a forward is an attacking player in football or hockey

explanation.surface: A naive striker who is prone to the odd game of cards.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: both mean uncomplicated and easy to follow.

clue.text: Factory making soldiers' best clothes

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army
finery is one's smartest dress

explanation.surface: A works that turns out dress uniforms for the troops.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: an industrial plant where oil or sugar is purified.

clue.text: Area within field sport that's evocative

indicators.note: within says the single letter goes inside the longer word

parts.note: hunting is one of the country pursuits called field sports

explanation.surface: A patch of ground on a playing pitch that stirs memories.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: both describe something that lingers poignantly in the mind.

clue.text: Mark is non-alcoholic, with sense

parts.note: a soft drink has no alcohol in it
touch is one of the five senses

explanation.surface: A man called Mark stays off the booze and shows good judgment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' looks like a name; in con artists' slang a mark is the victim picked out for a swindle.
explanation.definitionFit: A slang synonym: both mean a person who is easily conned or persuaded to part with money.

clue.text: Saves road repairs in the outskirts of Hastings

indicators.note: in puts the mended letters between the two edge letters
the outskirts of a town are its edges, so the first and last letters of the name
repairs means the letters are fixed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Money is kept back on mending the streets at the edge of a Sussex seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repairs' reads as a noun, roadworks; it is the verb that mends the letters into OARD, which 'in' places between 'the outskirts of' the Sussex seaside town's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym as a verb: stores things away rather than using them.

clue.text: Make an effort to put a couple of points and speak

parts.note: east and south are compass points, abbreviated E and S
to say something is to speak it

explanation.surface: Someone tries hard to make two arguments and have their voice heard.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal synonym as a verb: to attempt or try.

clue.text: Walk along the street then turn round

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street in addresses
to roll is to turn over and over

explanation.surface: Directions for an amble: go down the road and then come back.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to go on foot in a leisurely way.

clue.text: Bit of a shock to call time after half a mile

indicators.note: after puts the single letter behind the half word

parts.note: to ring someone is to telephone them

indicators.note: half a word is two of its four letters, here the second pair

explanation.surface: It is rather startling to stop a race when only half a mile has been run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half a' takes LE from mile and 'after' puts T behind it. A shock is a thick mass of hair, so a bit of one is a single curl.
explanation.definitionFit: A whimsical description: a shock is a mass of hair, and this is one curl of it.

clue.text: Look on a fellow as idle

parts.note: lo is an old exclamation meaning look
F is the abbreviation for fellow, as in FRS

explanation.surface: Regard a certain chap as lazy.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym as a verb: to laze about doing nothing.

clue.text: A source of trouble to overcome, taking a pessimistic view

indicators.note: the source of something is where it starts, so the word's opening letter

parts.note: to worst an opponent is to defeat them

explanation.surface: One cause of difficulty that a gloomy person has to get past.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: the phrase introduces the gloomiest possible outcome.

clue.text: Plays for which two eyes are oddly necessary

indicators.note: only the odd-numbered letters of the two words are needed

explanation.surface: Stage dramas that strangely demand a pair of eyes to watch.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym as a verb: a cat does this with a mouse.

clue.text: Belonged, but need a trip away …

indicators.note: away suggests the letters have gone astray from their places

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone who fitted in at home but still wants a holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym in the past tense: was a part of or related to something.

clue.text: … To recover from strokes

definitions.meaning: to pick up again after a setback, as a patient or a share price does
in tennis, a run of shots exchanged between the players before the point is won; the answer is singular for the whole exchange

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to pick up after a setback; as a noun it is a tennis exchange of shots.
